With it cut, the Elo differential flips to Pantoja +74 (2141 to 2067) and his chin returns to +0.23. The exclusion costs Van 6.6pp, and he is still a clear favourite.

The model's two engines disagree here more than anywhere else on the card. The hand-tuned layer, which reads the composites directly, makes Pantoja a slight favourite at 51.4%. The GBM, which also weighs record, Elo and form, has Van at 72.8%, and the final number follows the GBM. The hand-tuned side moved because of Pantoja's recent-form profile. Weighted toward his last five years, his grappling composite reads +1.61 (+0.87 on the career-weighted basis), his sub threat 1.46 against Van's -0.71, and his wrestling defence +0.81. Van's edge is still output: +2.19, the best output composite on the card, built over 145 UFC minutes at full trust, with power +0.90. Pantoja's output reads +0.18, and the decision edge has shrunk to a near-neutral +0.14. Age is part of the gap: Pantoja is 36.4 (age factor 0.89), Van 24.9. In past fights where the engines split this widely, results landed nearer the middle than either end, which here is about 61% Van.

Van's weakness is real and the model sees it. His chin reads -1.18 and he absorbs 3.9 head strikes per minute, which is why Pantoja's KO threat (1.25) is higher than Van's own (0.57). The sim still gives Pantoja only 5.7% by knockout. His better route is the back: 8.9% by submission, a third of his 26.9%. That figure is capped by the moneyline rather than by the grappling read: with the GBM making Van close to a 3-to-1 favourite, Pantoja wins only about one sim in four, and one in three of those wins is a submission. His last three wins came on the ground or on the cards (Kara-France and Asakura by submission, Erceg over five). Van's path is volume to a decision (43.6%) or a stoppage (27.5% by KO; the Taira fight ended in round five). synopsis.body: With the injury stoppage removed, the model scores the rematch as the fight the first one should have been: a 24-year-old volume striker with the best output profile on the card against a 36-year-old former champion with the best recent grappling in the fight. The cut flips Elo to Pantoja and restores his chin, and on the recent-form composites the hand-tuned layer even makes him a slight favourite. The GBM disagrees, and Van's pace carries the final number to 73.1%, most of it on the scorecards. The engines split more here than anywhere on the card, so read Van as a clear but not overwhelming favourite (nearer 61% if you split the difference). Pantoja's live paths are the submission and Van's leaky chin (-1.18).

matchupAnalysis: Despaigne 51.1%, the closest fight on the card and the one pick that changed sides in this re-run. Both of the model's layers take Despaigne: the hand-tuned layer clearly (83.1%), the GBM more narrowly (57.8%), and the final number lands just on his side. Elo still sides with Tuivasa by 159 points (1500 to 1341), but his 1500 is the residue of six straight losses, the last four being Marcin Tybura (a round-one submission) and three decisions to Jairzinho Rozenstruik, Tallison Teixeira and Louie Sutherland. Despaigne's 1341 comes from only three UFC bouts (1-2).

What moved is Tuivasa's profile. The model now weights each fighter's last five years more heavily, and Tuivasa's last five years are the skid: his output composite reads -1.81, the worst on the card, and his power +0.38, both well down on the career-weighted readings that made him a narrow favourite. The rest is poor too: grappling -0.91, chin -0.95 with a 0.66 chin-damage modifier. Despaigne's case is physical. At 6'7" he has a 213.4cm reach to Tuivasa's 190.5cm (reach +2.23 to -0.98), a decision edge of -1.91 in his favour, and the fight's best KO threat (1.61; Tuivasa's is -0.33). Against that sits how little, and how long ago, Despaigne has shown anything: 30 minutes of UFC evidence (trust 0.43), age 38.0 (age factor 0.85), and no fight since October 2024, 696 days, the only layoff on the card long enough to draw a penalty (layoff factor 0.91). His two UFC losses were both decisions, after a first-round knockout of Josh Parisian.

Both routes run through a knockout. Tuivasa wins 29.4% by KO (seven of his eight UFC wins came that way), Despaigne 26.1%, and Despaigne is also the likelier winner on the cards (20.2% to 14.9%). Only 35.0% go the distance and 37.6% end in round one. The blended O/U has Over 1.5 at 53.4% and Over 2.5 at 39.1%. Despaigne's record was refreshed to 6-2 before this run.

synopsis.body: The thinnest lean on the card, and the one that flipped when the model moved to recent-form composites. Tuivasa's six-fight skid now weighs on his output and power, and both layers side with Despaigne's reach and KO threat, even discounted for a 38-year-old coming off nearly two years out with 30 UFC minutes to his name. Despaigne 51.1%: a coin flip with a slight lean. Expect it to be short: nearly two-thirds of simulations end inside the distance.

The model barely knows Yoo: two UFC fights, 5.8 minutes, trust 0.08, so his composites sit near the prior. The Santos knockout loss now counts toward his composites (catchweight bouts had been left out of the composite inputs before this run), and his chin reads -0.54. Both men's pre-UFC rows were 0-0 placeholders before this run. They were backfilled from Sherdog (Aswell 10-2, Yoo 8-0), so both fighters' pre-UFC features now reflect real records. synopsis.body: A modest lean (58.1%) built on very little UFC evidence. Aswell has the knockout power and 62 minutes of UFC evidence, but a 1-4 record. Yoo has an unbeaten regional career and almost no UFC sample. If Aswell lands, he is the likelier finisher; if not, a Yoo decision is the single most likely result.
